ensembl.vep.render.chart module#

Charts as inline SVG.

Replaces the Google Charts the old VEP summary loaded from a CDN, so a report opens offline. The legend matches ensembl-client’s legend component: a 10px square marker, 12px from its label.

ensembl.vep.render.page module#

A self-contained HTML page.

Mirrors the information architecture of VEP’s summary page – a masthead, a fixed side menu of anchors, then one section per topic – with the Ensembl skin and no external requests. Everything the page needs is inlined, so it opens from a filesystem with no network.

class ensembl.vep.render.page.Section(*, identifier, title, blocks=(), group='')[source]#

Bases: object

One anchored block of the page.

Variables:

  • identifier (str) – The anchor, and what the side menu links to.

  • title (str) – The heading, and the menu entry.

  • blocks (tuple[str, ...]) – Ready-made HTML fragments – a table, a chart, a graph – laid out side by side.

  • group (str) – Optional heading grouping consecutive entries in the side menu.

ensembl.vep.render.report module#

A report: titled sections of tables and charts, rendered to one of three formats.

The one place a run summary, a fact profile, or any later report becomes HTML, text or JSON. A producer describes what it has – headings, rows, labelled quantities – and never how it should look, which is what lets it live outside this package without a renderer of its own.

ensembl.vep.render.theme module#

Ensembl’s design tokens.

Transcribed from the frontend source of truth, Ensembl/ensembl-client (src/styles/design-tokens.css), so refreshing the theme is a diff against one upstream file.

The design system is light-only: there is no prefers-color-scheme block, no data-theme and no dark token set anywhere upstream, so emitting one would invent a theme Ensembl does not have.

ensembl.vep.render.theme.stylesheet()[source]#

Return the theme as CSS, for inlining into a self-contained page.

Emits the tokens as custom properties on :root followed by the handful of element rules ensembl-client’s base.css sets, so a report matches the site without linking to it. Fonts are stacks only, with no @font-face: the site self-hosts its woff2 files, and linking them would stop the page opening offline.

Return type:

str
